title: The closed counit on abelian pro-etale sheaves
statement: Use [def-weil-size-convention], the pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let i:Z→X be an arbitrary closed immersion of schemes. On sheaves of abelian groups, the actual inverse-image/direct-image adjunction counit i*i_*→id is an isomorphism. Equivalently i_* is fully faithful. There is no quasi-compact-open-complement, qcqs-base, reducedness, or finite-presentation hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 09AA, 09BL and 09BK: closed immersions, affine closed-site lift and counit.

proof.text: Invertibility of the counit is local for affine open coverings of X and their inverse images in Z. Direct image commutes with open restriction by its base-change formula on sections. Identify the inverse images by adjunction; the mate comparisons transport the actual counit. Thus take X=Spec A and identify the closed immersion with Spec(A/I)→Spec A.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] to replace both pro-etale sites by their ind-etale affine bases, with the actual restriction equivalences on sheaves. These commute with the base-change direct images. The cocontinuous lift v and base change u of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties] satisfy v⊣u and have invertible unit by [lem-exc-closed-site-adjunction]. The opposite adjunction computes left Kan extension along u.op as precomposition with v.op, since in each indexing category the adjunction supplies the universal stage. Its subsequent sheafification is therefore inverse image. The resulting inverse-image comparison is the mate of the direct-image comparison and preserves the canonical counit.

For a closed-basis abelian sheaf G the presheaf computing i*i_*G is V↦G(u(v(V))). The inverse of the site unit identifies it naturally with G, via the contravariant sheaf map. It is already a sheaf. The canonical sheafification comparison is invertible, and the adjunction triangle identity identifies the induced map with the actual counit. Thus that counit is invertible on the basis and hence on the affine pro-etale site. All maps are additive, so the argument works directly for abelian sheaves.

The affine inverse counits agree on overlaps by naturality and uniqueness of inverses. Glue them to an inverse of the global counit. The empty closed scheme and nonreduced closed thickenings are included: the site unit and sheafification argument use neither points nor a radical or finitely generated defining ideal.

proof_origin.place: Tags 09AA and 09BL: affine basis, opposite closed-site adjunction and sheafification of G∘u.op∘v.op; global counit by affine descent.
